surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Hutson has three assists as the Canadiens get past the Devils
paras: It was a busy first period. Luke Evangelista got the scoring started for the Devils midway through the period, but Alex Newhook made it 1-1 for Montréal 40 seconds later. Timo Meier put the Devils back ahead 2-1 less than four minutes later, and that was all they would get. Nick Suzuki made it 2-2 for Montréal on the power play with 42 seconds left in the first. The Canadiens’ Zachary Bolduc left late in the second period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was listed as day to day with an upper-body injury. Jake Evans put the Habs ahead for good early in the third. Lane Hutson finished with three assists.

The Devils had a little more of the play, but the Canadiens had the finish. Jacob Fowler shook off a shaky start for the Canadiens, allowing two goals on the first eight shots and none on the last 22, and Connor Hellebuyck stopped 25 of 28 at the other end. It was Hellebuyck’s first loss of the season, after seven straight wins to open it. The Canadiens improved to 13-5-4, third in the Atlantic, while the Devils fell to 15-7-0, second in the Metropolitan.
